Interface OidcTokenRequest

All Superinterfaces:
edu.iu.IuRequestAttributes
public interface OidcTokenRequest extends edu.iu.IuRequestAttributes
A token request, as the transport that received it reports it.

One accessor per parameter OidcTokenEndpoint reads, so a caller adapting a servlet request, a JAX-RS request, or a test fixture never has to know how OAuth 2.0 spells them. Every accessor answers null when the request carried no such parameter; an adapter reports what arrived and validates nothing.

A token request is a form-encoded POST, so unlike an authorization request there is no query string to read from. The one thing that isn't a form parameter is the Authorization header, which is where an HTTP Basic client credential arrives.

IuRequestAttributes comes along because a refused request is logged against the address it came from, which is the only thing that identifies a caller whose credential didn't verify.

    • getClientAssertionIssuer

      String getClientAssertionIssuer()
      Gets the issuer the presented assertion claims, before anything has verified it.

      An assertion names its client in its own iss claim, so a request presenting one need not also name client_id. Reading that claim means decoding the assertion's payload as JSON, which an adapter's transport already does — the same reason authorization details arrive parsed rather than as a document.

      Unverified. It selects which registration the assertion is then verified against and nothing else, so a request naming a registration its assertion cannot satisfy fails at verification rather than here. An adapter answers null for an assertion it cannot decode or one claiming no issuer, both of which the endpoint refuses as a malformed assertion; it does not need to validate the claim beyond reading it.

      Returns:
      iss the assertion claims; null if no assertion was presented, or it cannot be decoded, or it claims no issuer

    • getAuthorization

      String getAuthorization()
      Gets the Authorization request header, verbatim.

      Reported as sent rather than decoded, since the endpoint has to tell an unsupported scheme from a malformed credential and both from none at all. A transport that decodes it here would collapse those.

      Returns:
      Authorization header; null if the request carried none

    • getRedirectUri

      String getRedirectUri()
      Gets the redirect_uri parameter, which selects the client endpoint the request is made through and, for an authorization code, must repeat the URI the code was issued to.
      Returns:
      redirect_uri; null if the request named none

    • getResource

      Iterable<String> getResource()
      Gets the resource parameter values.

      RFC 8707 allows the parameter to repeat, one value per resource the client wants the token usable at, so this reports every value rather than one.

      Returns:
      resource values in the order sent; null if the request named none
      See Also:
      • RFC 8707 §2

    • getScope

      String getScope()
      Gets the scope parameter, space-delimited as sent.

      Read only for client_credentials. A code or refresh grant carries the scope it was authorized with, and a redemption request doesn't get to widen or narrow it.

      Returns:
      scope; null if the request named none
